opts: Scarcely she had stepped outside when the storm began.
Scarcely had she stepped outside when the storm began.
Scarcely had she stepped outside than the storm began.
Scarcely did she stepped outside when the storm began.
questions.why: Scarcely + had + subject … when. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Identify the error: “The police has arrested the two suspects from the market.”
opts: The police
has arrested
the two suspects
from the market
questions.why: 'Police' is a plural noun, so 'have arrested'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: “He was ____ only person who knew the truth.”
opts: an
a
the
(no article)
questions.why: 'Only' is a limiting word and takes 'the'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “ubiquitous”:
opts: rare
found everywhere
ancient
unique
questions.why: Ubiquitous means present everywhere. GPSC-style practice item.

opts: Not only he arrived late, but he also forgot the files.
Not only did he arrived late, but he also forgot the files.
Not only arrived he late, but he also forgot the files.
Not only did he arrive late, but he also forgot the files.
questions.why: 'Not only' + did + subject + base verb. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “capricious”:
opts: steady
fickle
cruel
clever
questions.why: 'Capricious' means given to sudden changes of mood or behaviour; fickle. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the grammatically incorrect conditional sentence:
opts: If she would have studied, she would have passed.
If I had known, I would have told you.
If he comes, I will go with him.
If I were rich, I would travel.
questions.why: 'Would have' is not used in the if-clause: 'If she had studied'. GPSC-style practice item.

opts: He said, I will come tomorrow.”
He said; “I will come tomorrow.”
He said, “I will come tomorrow.”
He said. “I will come tomorrow.”
questions.why: A comma introduces the direct speech, which is enclosed in quotation marks. GPSC-style practice item.

opts: If I had known about the strike, I will have stayed at home.
Had I knew about the strike, I would have stayed at home.
Had I known about the strike, I would stay at home yesterday.
Had I known about the strike, I would have stayed at home.
questions.why: 'Had I known' = 'If I had known' (third conditional). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, “The earth moves round the sun.”
opts: The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moved round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth had moved round the sun.
The teacher told the earth moves round the sun.
questions.why: Universal truths keep the present tense. GPSC-style practice item.
